title: Meridian Freight / Halden Logistics - Discovery Call

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: Thanks for the time today, Linda, Marcus. We'd love to understand what's driving you to look at a new freight visibility platform.

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: Our biggest pain is status visibility - right now we get shipment updates over email from three different carriers, in three different formats, and our ops team manually reconciles them into a spreadsheet twice a day.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: From an IT side, we also want something that integrates with our existing warehouse management system rather than requiring double data entry.

transcript.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
transcript.text: Understood. On the visibility side, we support EDI 214 status updates from most major carriers, normalized into one feed. How many carriers do you work with today?

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: Five regularly, plus a few spot carriers for overflow capacity.

transcript.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
transcript.text: We already integrate with four of your five regular carriers. The fifth we'd need to onboard, which typically takes two to three weeks if they support standard EDI.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: On the WMS side, what integration options exist?

transcript.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
transcript.text: We have a REST API and prebuilt webhooks for shipment events. I'd need to know which WMS you're running to say more specifically.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: We're on a system called Freightline, custom-hosted.

transcript.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
transcript.text: I haven't personally integrated with Freightline before, so let me check with our integrations team on what's involved there rather than guess.

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: We'll get back to you on that by early next week.

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: That's fair. Timeline-wise, we're hoping to have something live within two months - is that realistic?

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: If the Freightline integration is straightforward, yes. If it needs custom work, it could push closer to three months. We'll know more once Yuki checks.

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: Understood. One more thing - pricing. Can you send over your standard pricing tiers so we can start budgeting?

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: Absolutely, I'll send that over today.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: And can we get a reference customer who's on a similar setup, ideally also using Freightline or something comparable?

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: I'll check who we can offer as a reference and follow up.

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: Great, let's plan to reconnect once you've looked into the Freightline question.

summary_key_points: Halden Logistics wants unified shipment visibility across five carriers instead of manually reconciling emails
Meridian already integrates with four of Halden's five carriers; the fifth would take two to three weeks to onboard
Halden's WMS is a custom-hosted system called Freightline, which Meridian hasn't integrated with before
Timeline depends on how complex the Freightline integration turns out to be

action_items.task: Check with the integrations team on what's involved in integrating with Halden's Freightline WMS
Send Halden standard pricing tiers today
Find and offer a comparable reference customer to Halden
Follow up with Halden early next week on the Freightline integration question

decisions: Reconnect for a follow-up call once the Freightline integration is scoped
open_questions: How complex will integrating with Halden's custom-hosted Freightline WMS be, and will it fit the two-month timeline?
Which carrier is Halden's fifth, and will it support standard EDI for onboarding?
